transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-09-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Evan Clarke (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sofia Gutierrez (Redwood Solutions), Marta Ruiz (CPO - Sentryline), Liam O'Connor (Head of Security), Aisha Khan (Cloud Eng), Ben Torres (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick compliance and onboarding review focused on region pinning/sovereign routing for EU workloads, KMS/escrow options, sub-processor mapping, RBAC/SSO integration, and next steps for a short PoC to validate latency and routing policies. Customer emphasized regulatory constraint for EU customer data and required audit trail for cross-border events.

Topics:
- Region pinning / sovereign routing (US vs EU)
- Subprocessor disclosure and onboarding timeframes
- KMS / encryption and key custody (bring-your-own-key vs Redwood-managed)
- RBAC, SSO integration (SAML/SCIM), audit logs and retention
- Fallbacks and model variant routing if capacity constrained

Transcript:
[00:00] Evan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick roll call and then we'll jump into the sovereign routing questions.
[00:14] Marta (Sentryline): Hi, Marta here, thanks. We have Liam, Aisha, Ben also on.
[00:18] Liam: Hey.
[00:20] Aisha: Hello.
[00:23] Ben: Hi all.
[00:25] Priya (Redwood): Hi, Priya from Redwood, I'll be the technical lead on the routing and KMS details.
[00:30] Evan: Great, so top level: Sentryline is looking to ensure EU customer payloads never leave EU datacenters and that any cross-border processing is auditable and approved. Is that a fair summary?
[00:38] Marta: Exactly. We have a mix of EU and US customers, but for EU contracts we have a binding clause that says processing must be within EU jurisdiction unless explicit consent/controls exist.
[00:48] Liam: We also need SOC 2 evidence and an ISO overview, plus a list of sub-processors that touch EU data.
[00:54] Sofia (Redwood): Totally — we can provide the SOC 2 Type II report and a concise ISO 27001 scope doc. We'll attach those.
[01:01] Marta: Good. On the routing piece, can you explain how Redwood pins region and what happens when capacity is low — like fallbacks?
[01:08] Priya: Sure. Our platform supports route policies that can be configured per-customer or per-tenant. You can set strict region pinning to a region group (e.g., eu-west+eu-central) so requests are only routed to nodes inside those regions. If strict pinning is enabled and capacity is exhausted, requests will queue or return a 429 depending on policy; we also support an automatic fallback to a compatible model that runs in the pinned region — the tricky case is when a model variant only exists in a different region.
[01:33] Aisha: Right that's the heart of it. We need to avoid silent cross-border fallback. Any fallback would need to be explicit and logged, and ideally require an approval flow.
[01:42] Priya: Absolutely. We can surface a policy flag: block_cross_border_fallback = true which returns an error rather than fallback. We also emit a routed_event log with a geo tag and decision reason when a fallback is attempted.
[01:53] Liam: On logging, retention and auditability: we need tamper-evident logs for routing decisions and key operations, with at least 2 years retention for EU-regulated flows. Do you support immutable audit logs or integration with our SIEM?
[02:04] Priya: Logs can be exported to customer-managed destinations — syslog, S3 (with EU region), or streaming to a SIEM using Kafka connectors. For immutability, we support WORM on S3 and can push to an append-only store; we also sign routing decision records with a HMAC so changes are detectable.
[02:20] Evan: To add, we keep a subprocessor inventory and we can provide per-region subprocessors — we won't route EU data to subprocessors located outside EU if strict region pinning is configured.
[02:29] Marta: Can you share what your subprocessors look like? Our legal needs a list for the DPA and we have a cutoff for monetary services vendors that are us-based.
[02:36] Evan: We'll share the subprocessor list; for EU-only deployments the stack is mostly cloud infra (GCP in EMEA regions) and a handful of CDN/logging partners. For any CRS — I mean, for any third-party model tuning or eval vendors, we treat them as subprocessors and can restrict them from EU tenant data.
[02:51] Ben: From procurement side — timeline wise, if Redwood can send SOC2 docs and subprocessor list this week, and if PoC goes well, we could sign a pilot contract in mid-October.
[03:02] Evan: Sounds reasonable. Priya, let's cover KMS next.
[03:05] Priya: KMS options: Redwood-managed keys (default), customer-managed keys (BYOK) via cloud KMS integrations (GCP KMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault), and a mediated escrow option for private deployments. With BYOK, keys never leave the customer's KMS — all encryption/decryption ops are proxied through the customer's KMS endpoints in the pinned region.
[03:25] Aisha: If we use BYOK, can you guarantee the cryptographic ops happen in EU? We need controls that the key material and KMS endpoints are EU-hosted.
[03:33] Priya: Yes — we support configuring the KMS endpoints to endpoints that reside in EU regions. For hosted Redwood, we will call your KMS endpoints; the crypto actually happens in the KMS within EU. We'll avoid returning plaintext outside EU. There are network egress caveats if you use cross-region replication, which you should disable.
[03:50] Liam: What about key rotation and access logs? We need key rotation events and KMS audit trail for compliance.
[03:56] Priya: We log all KMS requests, including signature material and request metadata, and can export to your SIEM. Rotation is supported; Redwood won't rotate customer-managed keys — that's controlled by the customer — but we can support a rotation handshake to re-encrypt caches when keys change.
[04:10] Marta: Cache — what about KV cache and prefix caching? We rely on caching for latency; we need to ensure cached prompt shards with EU PII remain in EU.
[04:18] Priya: Our KV cache can be region-scoped; for tenants with region-pinning we ensure cache nodes are deployed in the same region set. There was a small note: transcription sometimes shows KV as 'kay-v cash' so ignore that in the docs, that was me.
[04:30] Evan: (laughs) noted.
[04:32] Aisha: One more thing — subprocessor onboarding: we need a timeline and assurance we won't add new subprocessors affecting EU data without 30 days notice.
[04:40] Evan: Our DPA includes a 30-day notification for new subprocessors with an escalation path. For changes that affect region processing, we treat them as material changes and will require consent.
[04:50] Sofia: We can also provide an automated subprocessor feed — a changelog that your vendor management tool can poll.
[04:57] Ben: That helps procurement.
[04:59] Marta: On SOC2, can Redwood provide the SOC 2 Type II with the timeframe? We need it for our vendor due diligence.
[05:06] Evan: Yes — we can share the recent SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO 27001 certificate summary, redacted for sensitive material. We'll include scope lines that indicate hosted vs private deployments.
[05:16] Liam: For RBAC and SSO: we use Okta and enforce SCIM for user provisioning and SAML for SSO. We also enforce least privilege. Can Redwood integrate?
[05:25] Priya: Yes — Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. We have fine-grained RBAC controls in the Console and API keys can be scoped to datasets and model routes. We recommend service accounts with short-lived tokens for automation.
[05:38] Aisha: Can audit logs include user identity (Okta ID) mapped to actions?
[05:43] Priya: We include actor identity in audit entries when actions are performed through the Console or API; when using API keys we attach the key owner metadata and can correlate via SCIM user mapping.
[05:53] Liam: Regarding data residency audits: if an auditor requests proof of where a particular request was served, can you provide a signed audit record with the routing decision and the node ID and region?
[06:02] Priya: Yes, we can produce a signed record including request id, tenant id, timestamp, region, node id, and the decision rationale. We sign the record with our HMAC key; for higher assurance customers we can also incorporate timestamping via a third-party notary service.
[06:15] Marta: That would be ideal. Also, what's the expected lead time for a VPC/private deployment if we decide to do a private plane?
[06:22] Evan: For a private control plane in a customer VPC we typically plan 8–12 weeks for onboarding — shorter if we reuse our standard templates and infra. On-prem is longer.
[06:31] Ben: Budget question — is there an additional fee for BYOK and region-locked routing?
[06:36] Evan: BYOK is typically included for enterprise plans but there may be a setup fee and a higher SLA tier. Region-locked dedicated capacity is priced based on reserved GPU pools and region premiums. We'll provide a pricing sketch in the follow-up.
[06:47] Priya: One operational note: for strict pinning we recommend capacity reservations for peak windows to avoid fallbacks — you can set autoscale with a safety buffer, or Redwood Dedicated nodes pinned to your tenant.
[06:58] Liam: Good. For our audit we also require proof that no ML tuning vendors accessed EU PII. How do you segregate data for tuning/evals?
[07:06] Priya: We segregate training/eval datasets and require explicit opt-in per dataset. For EU tenants we can disable any customer data being used for model improvement by default. Any external tuning vendors are only given synthetic or redacted data behind NDAs and only if explicitly allowed.
[07:20] Marta: That covers most of it. Could you outline the PoC we discussed — what's the minimal set to validate region pinning and KMS?
[07:29] Priya: PoC plan: 1) Provide a small set of EU-only endpoints and a sample workload; 2) Redwood deploys a test tenant with strict region pinning and BYOK to your GCP KMS in europe-west3; 3) Run traffic for 48 hours with mixed loads and capture routing/audit logs; 4) Validate logs, signed routing decisions, and latency; 5) If everything passes, we scale to a small dedicated pool. We'll prepare a runbook.
[07:54] Aisha: For step 2, we'll need network allowlists for Redwood egress to our KMS endpoints and a test key.
[08:01] Priya: We'll send the IP ranges and an allowlist template.
[08:04] Ben: Who's the internal owner for the PoC on Redwood?
[08:07] Evan: Priya will lead tech and I'll coordinate contractual and compliance artifacts.
[08:11] Priya: I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the PoC kickoff.
[08:15] Marta: Any competitors we should be aware of — our security team evaluated AxiomCloud and EdgeServe — their claims on region pinning seemed weaker.
[08:21] Evan: We often get compared to AxiomCloud; their routing is more coarse-grained. We'll include a brief comparison slide.
[08:27] Sofia: Quick note on subprocessor notices: we'll include the automated changelog feed and also a signed CSV export for legal.
[08:33] Liam: Great. Two small questions before we wrap: can Redwood PII redaction be enforced at ingress? And can we have test harness requests that demonstrate not leaving EU?
[08:42] Priya: We have an ingress redaction option (regex-based plus entity detectors) you can enable per-tenant. For the harness, yes — we'll provide signed transcripts of the test requests and routing decisions proving locality.
[08:53] Marta: Perfect. Sounds like we have a path forward.
[08:56] Evan: To recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO and subprocessor list by Thursday; Priya will schedule PoC baseline and send allowlist/IPs; Sentryline will share EU data flows and tenancy map. We'll target PoC kickoff week of 2027-09-20.
[09:12] Ben: Procurement will prepare vendor questionnaire — I'll follow up with required fields.
[09:16] Evan: Thank you all. We'll follow up via email with the artefacts.
[09:20] Marta: Thanks everyone.

(End of recording)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional ASR mislabels and small word swaps (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "kay-v cash"), some timestamps approximate.

Attachments referenced: SOC2_TypeII_redacted.pdf (will be shared), ISO27001_scope.pdf, subprocessor_changelog_link (automated feed), PoC_runbook_draft_link
